name: Friction Removal
causal_claim: For recurring household organization failures, precise fit guidance and a maintainable low-complexity system can create value by removing decisions and rework rather than by selling more storage capacity.
why_it_might_work: Household organization problems are broad, recurring, and tied to finding items, reducing clutter, time, motivation, and storage constraints.
Dimensions, visibility, interoperability, and routine maintenance create observable decision criteria.
Compact nonregulated goods can support lean fulfillment and no-inventory validation.

supporting_evidence.proposition: A 2025 YouGov poll found insufficient storage, excess belongings, difficulty letting go, motivation, time, and not knowing where to start among reported organization challenges.
supporting_evidence.interpretation_limit: The poll establishes self-reported pain, not purchase intent or product economics.

supporting_evidence.proposition: The same poll reports broad use of bins, shelving, hooks, and drawer dividers, demonstrating existing solution behavior.
supporting_evidence.interpretation_limit: Use of current solutions does not show dissatisfaction or willingness to switch.

contradicting_evidence.proposition: Many organization failures may arise from possession volume, motivation, or household behavior rather than a missing product.
contradicting_evidence.interpretation_limit: The poll does not identify which respondents would benefit from a physical solution.

contradicting_evidence.proposition: High supplier availability may make physical organization products easy to copy and difficult to differentiate profitably.
contradicting_evidence.interpretation_limit: No supplier, price, contribution-margin, or return-rate sample has been collected.

required_conditions: One recurring friction must transfer across multiple room or life-stage contexts.
The mechanism must reduce decisions, time, or rework rather than only add capacity.
Fit can be verified through measurements and clear self-service constraints.
A compact, nonfragile, noncustom solution space exists with low support burden.
failure_conditions: The root problem is accumulation or motivation and a product merely relocates clutter.
Each useful solution requires custom dimensions or installation.
Customers accept fit failures because commodity prices are too low to support guidance.
The dominant solutions are bulky enough that shipping and returns destroy the economics.

falsification_experiment.question: Does a recurring, measurable household friction exist that fit certainty and a maintainable system can resolve across contexts?
falsification_experiment.hypothesis: The same fit, access, visibility, or maintenance failure appears in authorized reviews and actual household workarounds across multiple room types.
falsification_experiment.null_hypothesis: Organization failures are primarily behavioral or context-specific, leaving no transferable low-complexity commercial mechanism.
evidence_sources: At least 100 authorized or user-provided reviews across closet, drawer or cabinet, and general storage contexts and at least two sources.
Five structured household interviews with photographs or measurements supplied only with participant permission.
sampling_plan: Remove duplicates and preserve dimensions, context, claimed capacity, rating, and source where available.
Predeclare fit, access, visibility, durability, assembly, maintenance, and excess-capacity themes.
Ask households to demonstrate the current workaround and last failed attempt before discussing solutions.
survival_criteria: At least one actionable theme appears in 15 or more nonduplicate reviews, across all three contexts and both sources.
At least three of five households independently demonstrate the same friction in an actual current workaround.
The problem can be specified with self-service measurements and does not require custom installation.
falsification_criteria: No friction transfers across evidence sources and room contexts.
Observed failures are principally excess possessions or motivation rather than a solvable system defect.
Useful resolution requires custom sizing, bulky fulfillment, or ongoing human design service.
known_confounders: Before-and-after enthusiasm may fade after the observation period.
Review samples may overrepresent poor measurement and assembly errors.
A visually satisfying concept may not improve long-term maintenance behavior.
prohibited_actions: No scraping, advertising, inventory, supplier outreach, home entry, or collection of unnecessary personal images.
falsification_experiment.next_decision: Reject the mechanism or advance one cross-context friction to a no-inventory fit-and-choice test.

confidence_rationale: Broad consumer pain and existing solution use are observed, but product-level dissatisfaction, willingness to pay, and maintainability remain untested.

boundary_conditions: The first instance excludes custom installations, furniture, fragile goods, and bulky rigid storage.
transferability.next_replication_test: After one instance passes, repeat the same friction-removal mechanism in a distinct household workflow with new participants.
